### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/comments/reactions/:id (route, a path literal in a comment in objects))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/comments/reactions/:id (route, a path literal in a comment in objects))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41b64bb08cfe62ebc9dcb3459169daa383406b23` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `10518249fe0daf63704697606cf6476ddc76f18d` — the merge of head `fb45426a1e27984a2ff1ac09c1937ea77a054937` into base `41b64bb08cfe62ebc9dcb3459169daa383406b23`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 10518249fe0daf63704697606cf6476ddc76f18d && git checkout 10518249fe0daf63704697606cf6476ddc76f18d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 41b64bb08cfe62ebc9dcb3459169daa383406b23 fb45426a1e27984a2ff1ac09c1937ea77a054937 && git checkout -B drift-repro 41b64bb08cfe62ebc9dcb3459169daa383406b23 && git merge --no-ff fb45426a1e27984a2ff1ac09c1937ea77a054937

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41b64bb08cfe62ebc9dcb3459169daa383406b23
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 41b64bb08cfe62ebc9dcb3459169daa383406b23` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Request: review · area E1 · head 799041bdf8fc66f156895d3c3ff91d11d6040cc1 · 2026-11-15T03:20Z

Verification update: since this PR was opened, the cli unit tier (420/420 files) and the full dogfood battery (467 passed / 3 skipped files, 3954 passed / 42 skipped tests) finished green locally on this head; the body lists them as running / not measured.

## Review — changes needed

Head-sha: `799041bdf8fc66f156895d3c3ff91d11d6040cc1`
Reviewed-by: session_016WV4cwxS1ZpSu2hAMRcqbt (review#1, area-lease pilot E1)

**must-fix 1: Clause-② is `yes (widening)`, not `no`.** A published default, the stock `member_default` set, now admits requests a stock member was refused before. `POST` and `GET /api/v1/data/sys_comment_reaction` go from 403 to 201/200. That is a door's accept set widening (ADR-0150's Clause-② reading covers "a door's request or response"). It is also the repo's precedent: `32641-sys-user-ai-readable` and #32442 both declared `yes (widening)` for a member grant. Change the line in the changeset and in the PR body. `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` stay; no authorable-surface or defaults shard moves.

**should-fix 2: pin the unfiltered list read.** The dogfood cases read the data door only with a `comment_id` filter. Add one CONTROL: an unfiltered `GET /data/sys_comment_reaction` as a member, asserting that the reaction on the unreadable comment is absent. The engine-level pin exists (`comment-reaction-access.integration.test.ts`). The stock grant now makes the door's own answer the one to pin.

**Security, checked and sound**
- Read: the plugin-audit read middleware (`comment-access-hooks.ts`, `computeReactionVisibilityFilter`) keeps only rows whose comment the caller can read, on find, findOne, count and aggregate. It denies the read if it cannot resolve that set.
- Create: `authorizeReactionInsert` overwrites `user_id` with the session user and refuses a comment the caller cannot read, row by row on `createMany`. `created_by` is server-stamped.
- Delete: there is no delete bit, so the data door refuses. Unreact goes through `DELETE /comments/reactions/:id`, which refuses unless `created_by` is the caller. No door removes another member's reaction.
- `external_default` is untouched and is resolved instead of `member_default` for external users. Your CONTROL pins that.
- nit, already existing and not this PR's to fix: without a middleware seam, plugin-audit only warns and does not install the read gate (`audit-plugin.ts`). Every member now reaches that case. That is worth a loose-ends line if anyone runs a seamless engine.

**VERDICT: changes needed** (must-fix 1; should-fix 2). A full contract-review record follows on the fixed head, since this PR is Clause-② yes.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `fb45426a1e27984a2ff1ac09c1937ea77a054937`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (Clause-② yes, no spec or governed path). Second round: `fb45426a` over `799041bd` (my changes-needed 6888529912) changes only the changeset's Clause-② line and adds one dogfood CONTROL.

### ① Derived judgments

- `member_default` gains `sys_comment_reaction` with read and create and no edit or delete. `external_default` is unchanged, and external users resolve it instead of `member_default`.
- Read: the plugin-audit read middleware (`computeReactionVisibilityFilter` in `comment-access-hooks.ts`) keeps only rows whose comment the caller can read, on find, findOne, count and aggregate. It denies the read when it cannot resolve that set. The new CONTROL pins this at the data door: an unfiltered member list answers 200 with the member's own reaction and without the reaction on the unreadable comment, while that row exists in the database.
- Create: `authorizeReactionInsert` overwrites `user_id` with the session user and refuses a comment the caller cannot read, row by row. `created_by` is stamped by the server.
- Delete: there is no delete bit, so the data door refuses. Unreact goes through `DELETE /comments/reactions/:id`, which refuses unless `created_by` is the caller. No door removes another member's reaction, and a dogfood case pins that.
- Pins: a unit pin of every materialized bit, with an `external_default` CONTROL; the dogfood cases react 201, unreact own, are refused on another member's reaction, read only readable comments, and run the unfiltered-list CONTROL. One ablation turned the unit pin and the dogfood cases red with 403.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: a stock member's `POST` and `GET /data/sys_comment_reaction` go from 403 to 201/200. That is a door's accept set widening, on the precedent of `32641-sys-user-ai-readable` and #32442. `Metadata-protocol: none`: a shipped permission set, with no authorable key or default moved and no shard moved. `@objectstack/plugin-security` stays at `patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security-relevant (a stock grant), checked above. No finding.
- nit, already present before this PR and not this PR's to fix: on an engine with no middleware seam, plugin-audit only warns and does not install the reaction read gate (`audit-plugin.ts`). Every member can now reach that case.
- No governed path; not Tier H. Land on this head's own green CI.
